initial_observations.claim: Both pinned sources present a deep hooked bill, swept layers behind the brow, a circular optic embedded in surrounding plated structure, and a shaped open cheek/mandible relationship. The retained head views instead show a broad pale smooth top shell, a thick projecting optic ring, and sparse disconnected strips around the cheek.

The locked full bird has irregular edged and fastened regional plates and dense visible joint/hardware accents. The retained whole birds read smoother, with repeated rounded overlapping breast/wing plates and simpler rod-like leg presentation. Camera, pose and illumination differ, so this is qualitative appearance comparison rather than metrology.

Retained builder and Mechanic views keep the same avian stance, curved neck, compact folded shield-wing and separated toes. Their clearest visible era difference in these supplied pairs is the bright versus dark optic; broader finish distinction is not conspicuous.

These six images do not establish Maker finish, motion continuity, rear/opposite-side fidelity, native/export preservation, or improvement relative to earlier checkpoints. The July body's wing span and pose are excluded from this comparison because its authorized scope is head identity.

A connected head proposal is likely to deliver greater recognizable change than another isolated crown color adjustment; regional plate and era-finish work should remain visible follow-ons rather than disappear behind that head scope.
